reviewed_items.reviewer_notes: All 3 gates passed. The spec deviation is confirmed: middleware (L38-40) short-circuits with `NextResponse.next()` for STEM OAuth sessions without calling `updateSession`, so no Supabase JWT is established and `auth.uid()` is always null for STEM OAuth users. An attacker can trigger this via a STEM OAuth-authenticated HTTP request by calling `getUserRecentAttendance(victimId)` with a victim's userId, relying on the broken RLS backstop (`auth.uid() = user_id` evaluates to `null = user_id` = false for all rows) — concrete IDOR is partially mitigated by `REVOKE ALL ON attendance.attendances FROM anon` in migration `20260317000001_fix_security_permissions.sql`, but the root vulnerability (absent Supabase session for all STEM OAuth users) affects the entire authenticated surface area and exploitability depends on migration application state and other tables with looser anon grants.
